scenarios.name: Merge an Eligible Pull Request - Scenario 2
Close or Reopen a Pull Request Without Merging - Scenario 1
Close or Reopen a Pull Request Without Merging - Scenario 2

REQ-6-1 counts only a reviewer's latest decision and states that any valid Request changes blocks merging; the merge area of a blocked PR must therefore offer no actionable merge control. Fixture: the seeded Open PR acme-docs#1 targets protected main with both toggles enabled, its current compare commit c-acme-3 carries a valid non-author approval (bob-reviewer) and test: success, and dana-dev — granted the minimal Write permission a reviewer needs — has one non-stale 'Changes requested' review on that same commit. The real merge-area renderer APP.pullSidebar derives eligibility from the approval count alone and never consults Request changes, so it emits an actionable Merge pull request button. Corrected from the failing version: the module-level escaping helper (var esc = ARC.esc) had no ARC.esc provided, so the renderer threw 'esc is not a function'; the fixture now supplies that escaping plumbing, which is external rendering plumbing, not the rule under test.

REQ-6-5 requires that on a protected target each enabled rule is enforced independently, so an Open PR with a valid non-author approval but a `test` check that is not success stays blocked and shows a disabled Merge pull request button plus the unmet-condition explanation. Fixture: seeded PR acme-docs#1 targets protected main with both Require 1 approval and Require status check test enabled; bob-reviewer's approval is valid and non-stale for the current compare commit c-acme-3, no valid Request changes exists, and the check record for that same commit is 'pending'. APP.pullSidebar (the real merge-area renderer) computes ok from pr.status and the approval rule only and never reads the check rule, so it renders an actionable Merge pull request control for a PR that the protection rule requires to be blocked. Corrected from the failing version: ARC.esc (the external escaping plumbing consumed by the module-level esc helper) is now supplied in setup so the renderer can run.

REQ-6-3-3 requires that a draft started with Start a review stays pending: it is shown with 'Pending review' to its author but is not made public before review submission. Fixture: the seeded Open PR acme-docs#1 is viewed by alice-dev (its author, a different account from the commenter bob-reviewer) and the Files changed store holds one already-published inline comment plus one unsubmitted (published:false) inline comment by bob-reviewer on the same current compare commit c-acme-3. APP.pullFiles, the real Files-changed renderer, lists every inline record of the PR without any author or publication check, so bob-reviewer's unsubmitted draft body is rendered to alice-dev and thus becomes public before submission. Corrected from the failing version: ARC.esc (the external escaping helper consumed by the module-level esc binding) is supplied in setup, and the fixture explicitly clears ui().lineEditor so the diff-line rendering path used here runs.

REQ-5-3-1 defines assignable members as accounts holding at least Triage permission on the current repository and states that non-assignable users do not appear in the results. In the seed, carol-reader is an organization member of acme-demo but holds only a direct Read grant on acme-docs (her only team is frontend-child, which has no grant and team hierarchy is not transitive), so the application's own predicate APP.canTriage(repo, carol-reader) is false, while bob-reviewer (direct Write) and the signed-in Owner are eligible. The picker renderer that the issue detail page is meant to show filters candidates by organization membership instead of repository permission, so it offers carol-reader as an assignable option. Corrected from the rejected version: the picker is declared inside the actions object, so it must be selected by its full declaration path APP.actions.assigneePicker (the runner reported APP.assigneePicker does not exist); ARC.esc and the ARC.route resolution used by the picker are supplied as external plumbing.
